name: Pu-erh Tea
description: A deeply earthy aged fermented tea from Yunnan, compressed into cakes and brewed in small clay teapots.
ingredients: a handful of fresh scallion greens, chopped
a drizzle of toasted sesame oil
a generous spoonful of black vinegar
instructions: Combine the glutinous rice and water in a saucepan, blender, or pitcher, stirring well.
Add the chili oil and black vinegar, stirring gently so their flavor infuses the mixture.
Heat gently over low heat (or blend, or steep, depending on the drink) until well combined and fragrant, about 5 mins.
Strain through a fine sieve to remove any solids, if needed.
Sweeten to taste with toasted sesame oil, adjusting gradually until the balance feels right.
Chill in the refrigerator, or pour straight over ice, depending on whether it is served cold or hot.
Garnish with scallion greens just before serving.
tips: Adjust the sweetness gradually, tasting as you go — you can always add more toasted sesame oil, but you cannot take it away.
If serving warm, gently reheat just before pouring rather than letting it come to a boil.
